decisions.reason: The candidate already records the same-message issuance of four Small Block and three Big Block tickets. The lifecycle change affects how issued tickets persist and reset, not their issuance quantity or recipient.
The candidate already records the same-message requirement to display both ticket counters and permanent badges. The revised ticket lifecycle does not remove or alter those metadata fields.

The candidate already records the same-message pool trigger and royalty contribution rule. Ticket eligibility, burning, and reset behavior belongs to the separate ticket-lifecycle Requirement and leaves the Small Block prize values unchanged.

The candidate already records the same-message Big Block pool target and draw condition. The ticket reset policy changes ticket lifecycle state without changing the recorded prize count, amount, pool target, or trigger.
The source explicitly says the one-ticket allocation to a random existing NFT remains the same, and the candidate already records that same-message rule.
The source explicitly states that prize claims remain manual, which is already recorded by the candidate. Ticket expiration and reset behavior does not change the claim flow.
The source explicitly states that the automatic $10 commission remains unchanged, and the candidate already records that same-message commission rule.
The prize-ticket lifecycle adjustment has no semantic effect on the product name or future branding state.
